products: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.title: Public Preview: SQL performance monitoring for SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.description:
The public preview of Microsoft-managed performance monitoring for SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines is now available. You can now monitor SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines without building custom collection scripts or correlating telemetry across disconnected tools. The SQL IaaS Agent extension collects performance data from your SQL Server instances and sends it to a Microsoft-managed telemetry pipeline for processing and storage. 

Resource-level and estate-wide dashboards help you identify performance trends, anomalies, and resource bottlenecks. Integration with Fabric Database Hub brings this telemetry into a unified monitoring experience. For deeper analysis and custom visualizations, you can securely query your data with Kusto Query Language through an RBAC-protected Azure Data Explorer proxy endpoint. 

Learn more:  

  • Documentation  
  • Announcement blog

items.title: Retirement: NVv3-series Azure Virtual Machines
items.description:
On September 30, 2026, Microsoft Azure retired the Standard_NV12s_v3, Standard_NV12hs_v3, Standard_NV24s_v3, Standard_NV24ms_v3, Standard_NV32ms_v3, and Standard_NV48s_v3 virtual machines (VMs) in the NVv3-series VMs.

Any remaining NVv3-series VMs will be set to a deallocated state. They'll stop working and no longer incur billing charges. NVv3 will no longer be under SLA or have support included. 

Note: 1-year and 3-year Reserved Instance (RI) purchases for the NVv3-series ended on November 2, 2025.

Note: If you're currently using NVv3-series Azure VMs in the Azure UAE North region, you can continue using the NVv3-series VMs beyond the general retirement date of September 30, 2026 until the extension date of January 31, 2027. Customers in the Azure UAE North region must migrate off the NVv3-series VMs by January 31, 2027.

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: NVv4-series Azure Virtual Machines
items.description:
On September 30, 2026, Microsoft Azure retired the Standard_NV4as_v4, Standard_NV4ahs_v4, Standard_NV8as_v4, Standard_NV8ahs_v4, Standard_NV16as_v4, Standard_NV16ahs_v4, Standard_NV32as_v4, and Standard_NV32ahs_v4 virtual machines (VMs) in the NVv4-series VMs. 

Any remaining NVv4-series VMs will be set to a deallocated state. They'll stop working and no longer incur billing charges. NVv4 will no longer be under SLA or have support included. 

Note: 1-year and 3-year Reserved Instance (RI) purchases for the NVv4-series ended on November 2, 2025.

Note: All Compute Pre-Purchase (CPP) sales for the NVv4-series ended on June 2, 2026.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Ubuntu 26.04 support in AKS
items.description:
Teams running Ubuntu node pools on AKS need to stay current with Ubuntu LTS releases, but each OS transition can introduce package footprint, security, and compatibility concerns. Ubuntu 26.04 support introduces the Ubuntu2604 OS SKU using Ubuntu Minimal as the baseline image, while preserving existing AKS create, update, and node pool workflows. You get a smaller default host footprint, Linux LTS kernel 7.0, and a controlled migration path with rollback flexibility to Ubuntu 24.04 where supported.

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VMs
items.description:
As part of the Microsoft Azure VM lifecycle policy, Microsoft is announcing the retirement of the Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VM series in public cloud Azure regions. These VMs will enter the End-of-Life lifecycle stage and retire on November 15, 2029.

We know migrating production workloads takes planning and engineering time. To keep your applications and workloads running without interruption, migrate any Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, or Esv3 series VMs to a newer VM series before November 15, 2029. After this date, Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 virtual machines will enter the Retired lifecycle stage and will no longer be supported on Azure. Virtual machines not transitioned by that time may be deallocated and ultimately deleted as the underlying hardware and platform infrastructure are retired. We recommend evaluating available modernization options as soon as possible and moving to newer VM generations, such as Azure Dsv5 or Esv5v5 series virtual machines, to maintain uninterrupted service and gain improved performance, security, and reliability. 

Additionally, as previously communicated, as of July 1, 2026, one-year and three-year Reserved Instances (RIs) for the Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 VM series are no longer available for purchase or renewal. If you would like to continue commitment savings, we recommend reviewing your current reserved instance orders and if RIs are still in effect for these VMs, consider a trade-in of active reservations for Azure savings plan for compute contracts.  

Help and support  

Microsoft is committed to ensuring every customer navigates this transition quickly, successfully, and with clarity. Customers with an active support plan can submit a support request for technical assistance with migration planning and execution. For general questions, Microsoft Q&A provides access to community experts. 

Learn more:  

  • Azure Virtual Machines Lifecycle policy 
  • v5 modernization guide
